description: High sodium load from added salt and sodium-based additives
typical_food_sources: Table salt, papad, pickles, namkeen, processed meats, sauces, instant noodles, cheese
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Antagonises antihypertensives (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics, beta blockers); raises fluid retention with corticosteroids and NSAIDs

description: High potassium content or potassium-based salt substitutes
typical_food_sources: Bananas, coconut water, potatoes, spinach, dal, dried fruit, tomato paste, low-sodium salt
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hyperkalaemia risk with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, potassium-sparing diuretics, aldosterone antagonists, trimethoprim

description: Sucrose and other free sugars added during processing
typical_food_sources: Sugar, jaggery, honey, syrups, sweets, soft drinks, biscuits, jam
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Worsens glycaemic control on antidiabetics and insulin; interacts with steroid-induced hyperglycaemia

description: High-glycaemic starches and maltodextrin-type glucose polymers that spike blood glucose
typical_food_sources: Maida, white rice, cornflour, maltodextrin, dextrose, glucose syrup, sabudana
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Blunts glycaemic control on metformin, sulfonylureas, DPP-4/SGLT2 inhibitors, insulin

description: High saturated fat from tropical oils and dairy fat
typical_food_sources: Palm oil, palmolein, ghee, butter, coconut, cream, vanaspati, cheese
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Opposes statins/fibrates for lipid control; large fatty meals alter absorption of some drugs

description: Industrially produced trans fatty acids
typical_food_sources: Vanaspati, hydrogenated vegetable oil, some bakery shortening, older margarine
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Raises cardiovascular risk; works against statins and other lipid-lowering therapy

description: Vasoactive amine formed during fermentation and ageing
typical_food_sources: Aged cheese, soy sauce, fermented soy, cured/fermented meats, tank beer, yeast extract, overripe bananas
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hypertensive crisis with MAO inhibitors (incl. linezolid, procarbazine); caution with some antidepressants

description: Foods rich in vitamin K1/K2 that affect clotting
typical_food_sources: Spinach, kale, methi, other leafy greens, broccoli, cabbage, natto, green tea
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Reduces effect of vitamin-K antagonist anticoagulants (warfarin, acenocoumarol) if intake fluctuates

description: CYP3A4-inhibiting citrus compounds (grapefruit, pomelo, Seville orange)
typical_food_sources: Grapefruit, pomelo, Seville/bitter orange, some juices and marmalades
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Raises blood levels of many CYP3A4 substrates: statins, calcium channel blockers, some immunosuppressants, DOACs

description: Methylxanthine stimulant
typical_food_sources: Coffee, tea, cola, energy drinks, chocolate, guarana, some supplements
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Additive stimulation and raised levels with fluoroquinolones, theophylline, some antidepressants; opposes sedatives

description: High-oxalate foods that bind minerals and promote stones
typical_food_sources: Spinach, beetroot, nuts, sesame, tea, chocolate, rhubarb, sweet potato
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Reduces absorption of co-taken calcium/iron; stone risk with high-dose vitamin C and some diuretics

description: Di- and trivalent cations that bind drugs in the gut
typical_food_sources: Milk, curd, paneer, fortified foods, calcium-set tofu, ragi, iron-fortified cereals
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Chelates and blocks absorption of tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, levothyroxine, bisphosphonates, some HIV drugs

description: Ethanol as an ingredient or in beverages
typical_food_sources: Beer, wine, spirits, some sauces, vanilla/kheer flavourings, fermented preparations
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Disulfiram-like reaction with metronidazole/tinidazole; additive CNS depression with sedatives, opioids, antihistamines; hepatotoxicity with paracetamol; lactic acidosis with metformin

description: High biogenic histamine in fermented or poorly stored foods
typical_food_sources: Aged cheese, fermented soy, wine, cured fish, sauerkraut, idli/dosa batter
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Symptom flare with MAO inhibitors and some antihistamine regimens; overlaps with tyramine sources

description: Glycyrrhizin from licorice root causing pseudo-aldosteronism
typical_food_sources: Mulethi, licorice candy, some herbal teas, certain digestive mixes and pan masala
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Causes potassium loss and sodium retention; worsens hypertension control and amplifies hypokalaemia from diuretics and corticosteroids

description: High-purine foods raising uric acid
typical_food_sources: Organ meat, red meat, seafood, anchovies, meat extracts, some pulses, yeast extract
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Provokes gout flares and opposes urate-lowering therapy (allopurinol, febuxostat); interacts with thiazide-induced hyperuricaemia

description: Cow milk protein and milk-derived ingredients
typical_food_sources: Milk, milk solids, whey, casein, paneer, butter, ghee, cream, khoya
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hard-stop allergen; also a chelating calcium source (see calcium_mineral_chelation)

description: Soybean protein and soy-derived ingredients
typical_food_sources: Soy flour, soy protein, soy lecithin, soy sauce, tofu, textured vegetable protein
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hard-stop allergen; soy protein separately reduces levothyroxine absorption; fermented soy is a tyramine source

description: Peanut and tree nut proteins
typical_food_sources: Peanut, cashew, almond, walnut, pistachio, hazelnut, groundnut oil (cold-pressed)
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hard-stop allergen with anaphylaxis risk

description: Wheat/barley/rye gluten proteins
typical_food_sources: Wheat flour, maida, atta, semolina/suji, barley malt, wheat bran, seitan
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hard-stop for coeliac disease and wheat allergy; malt/barley also overlaps with other grains

description: Egg proteins
typical_food_sources: Whole egg, egg white, albumen, egg powder, lysozyme, mayonnaise
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hard-stop allergen; relevant to some vaccine and propofol cautions

description: Sesame seed protein
typical_food_sources: Til, sesame seeds, tahini, sesame oil, gingelly oil, some namkeen and bakery toppings
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hard-stop allergen, increasingly recognised for severe reactions

description: Finned-fish proteins
typical_food_sources: Fish, anchovy, sardine, fish sauce, surimi, fish extract, some Worcestershire sauce
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hard-stop allergen; anchovy/sardine are also purine sources

description: Crustacean and mollusc proteins
typical_food_sources: Prawn, shrimp, crab, lobster, crayfish, mussels, squid, oyster
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Hard-stop allergen with high anaphylaxis risk

description: Mustard seed protein
typical_food_sources: Mustard seed, mustard powder, rai, kasundi, mustard oil (cold-pressed), some pickles and mayonnaise
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Recognised allergen in EU/FSSAI labelling; ubiquitous in Indian cooking

description: Sulphur dioxide and sulphite preservatives (>10 ppm)
typical_food_sources: Dried fruit, bottled lemon/lime juice, pickles, some wines, processed potato, glucose syrup
why_it_matters_for_drugs: Triggers asthma/urticaria in sensitive people; INS 220-228
